You may be surprised to know that Kazakh: You may be surprised to learn that Kazakhstan, not the Netherlands, is the home of the tulip. Unlike in the Netherlands, where people gather to watch the annual display of these beautiful flowers, tulips in Kazakhstan grow and bloom in the wild without human intervention and cover vast areas. Here you can see about 40 of the 65 species of wild tulip found in Central Asia, 18 of which are listed as endangered. Among them are the Schrenck and Greig tulips, considered some of the most beautiful.

3. The black beach of Lake Alakol with t: 3. The black beach of Lake Alakol and its healing waters
If you are tired of the ubiquitous regul: If you are tired of the usual golden sandy beaches, it’s time to discover the black-pebble beach of Lake Alakol, which is located in south-eastern Kazakhstan. The lake not only has an unusual shoreline but also has healing powers. The black beach attracts people suffering from colds, skin diseases and nervous exhaustion, and all those who like to meditate. Even Soviet cosmonauts used to come to the lake to recuperate after their flights.
The Alakol Nature Reserve was created he: The Alakol Nature Reserve was created here to protect rare species of birds, and the famous silver perch can be found in the lake’s waters. If you come to the lake at the beginning of May, you can join the many birdwatchers who come for the “Wings of Alakol” festival. The event attracts not only birdwatchers but also journalists, yoga practitioners and musicians. This is how the season begins on Alakol. Then comes summer – the time of sun, swimming and fun on the water. In autumn there is another festival, held on the first weekend of September – “Okunkol”, where anglers catch the famous silver perch.
